headline: North Korea's Lazarus group turned the one actively exploited flaw in Microsoft's record August patch batch into defense-sector breaches, as a poisoned LiteLLM build and fresh SYSTEM-level exploits piled on.

emerging_trends.text: North Korea's Lazarus operators keep mining the hiring pipeline, posing as recruiters and burying a Windows zero-day inside a Lockheed Martin job decoy to reach defense contractors.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Lazarus Zero-Day Drives August Patch Tuesday

emerging_trends.text: Attackers increasingly poison the build chain itself, turning the Trivy scanner breach into rogue LiteLLM packages that scattered credential-stealing code across thousands of organizations.
Defenders have started planting prompt injections beside their cloud secrets, weaponizing an AI hacking agent's own guardrails to make it quit mid-attack.

topics.title: Lazarus Zero-Day Drives August Patch Tuesday
topics.latest_developments: Check Point, BleepingComputer, and SecurityWeek confirmed today that CVE-2026-68820, the lone actively exploited zero-day in Microsoft's August rollout, is the afd.sys WinSock use-after-free Lazarus wielded against defense firms, and researchers found it while dissecting the Operation Dream Job hiring lure.
topics.summary: The North Korean crew poses as recruiters, ships trojanized PDF software carrying a Lockheed Martin job decoy, and installs the ForestTiger backdoor; CISA gave U.S. federal agencies two weeks to patch.

sources.title: Lazarus hackers exploited Windows zero-day to target defense firms
Fresh Windows Zero-Day Exploited in North Korean Cyberattacks
CISA gives federal agencies two weeks to patch Microsoft bug exploited in DPRK campaign
Lazarus hackers pair fake job offers with Windows zero-day exploit

topics.title: ShieldBreak and Plug and Pwn SYSTEM Exploits
topics.latest_developments: A day after Patch Tuesday, the researcher Chaotic Eclipse released ShieldBreak, a proof-of-concept that bypasses the RoguePlanet fix CVE-2026-50656 in Microsoft Defender to reach SYSTEM, and a separate team disclosed Plug and Pwn, which abuses Windows Plug and Play to auto-install vulnerable vendor drivers for the same foothold.
topics.summary: Both techniques hand a local attacker full SYSTEM control on up-to-date Windows machines.

sources.title: New Microsoft Defender 'ShieldBreak' zero-day grants SYSTEM privileges
ShieldBreak Zero-Day PoC Claims Microsoft Defender Patch Bypass With SYSTEM Access
Plug and Pwn attack uses fake USB devices for Windows SYSTEM access

topics.title: SAP, Adobe, and Chipmaker Critical Patches
topics.latest_developments: SAP shipped a fix for CVE-2026-58231, a CVSS 10.0 unauthenticated remote code execution flaw in the Commerce Cloud Data Hub Adapter, and Intel and AMD together closed more than 80 chip vulnerabilities that enable privilege escalation and code execution, extending the week's critical-patch wave beyond Adobe's three CVSS 10.0 ColdFusion and Campaign Classic bugs.
topics.summary: Administrators should prioritize the unauthenticated, network-reachable flaws—SAP Commerce Cloud and Adobe ColdFusion CVE-2026-48362—ahead of the local chip fixes.

sources.title: SAP Commerce Cloud Flaw Could Let Unauthenticated Attackers Execute Arbitrary Code
Chipmaker Patch Tuesday: Intel, AMD Fix Over 80 Vulnerabilities Combined
Adobe Patches Three CVSS 10.0 ColdFusion and Campaign Classic Flaws

topics.title: Ransomware Strikes Government, Infrastructure, and Logistics
topics.latest_developments: The Gunra ransomware-as-a-service operation, built on leaked Conti code, exploited Fortinet firewall and VPN flaws and bypassed multifactor authentication against critical-infrastructure targets; ransomware crippled Colombia's Justice Ministry days before the country's presidential transition; and a cyberattack disrupted Ceva Logistics at eight European contract-logistics warehouses, delaying shipments.
topics.summary: Ransomware crews keep hitting government, critical infrastructure, and supply-chain operators; organizations should patch Fortinet appliances, enforce phishing-resistant MFA, and isolate backups.

sources.title: Gunra Ransomware Gang Exploits Fortinet Flaws, Bypasses MFA
Ransomware Hits Colombian Justice Ministry Days Before Presidential Transition
Ceva Logistics Operations Disrupted by Cyberattack

topics.title: LiteLLM Supply Chain Compromise
topics.latest_developments: SecurityWeek and The Hacker News reported that two malicious LiteLLM releases sat on PyPI for roughly 40 minutes in March after the Trivy compromise, and CloudSEK's dataset of about 434,000 stolen files now maps exposure to more than 2,100 organizations.
topics.summary: The trojanized builds harvested cloud keys, SSH keys, Kubernetes tokens, and database passwords from every system that installed them; affected users must rotate all secrets.

sources.title: Over 2,500 Organizations Impacted by LiteLLM Supply Chain Attack
Malicious LiteLLM Releases Tied to Trivy Hack May Have Exposed 2,100+ Organizations

topics.title: Prompt Injections Turned Into Defense
topics.latest_developments: Bruce Schneier highlighted Tracebit research showing that placing prompt injections alongside passwords and cryptographic keys stored in Amazon Web Services often stops AI hacking agents cold, because the planted text orders the attacking model to break its own guardrails and it shuts down.
topics.summary: The technique turns an autonomous attack agent's safety training into a tripwire defenders can plant beside their secrets.
